courses.title: Elementary Mathematics (MTH 101)
courses.description: Sets, indices and logarithms, equations, sequences and basic calculus for 100 Level science and health students.

topics.title: Sets and Number Systems
topics.summary: Set notation, operations, Venn diagrams and the real number system.

material.heading: Sets
material.body: A set is a well-defined collection of objects. A ∪ B (union) contains elements in A or B; A ∩ B (intersection) contains elements in both; A′ (complement) contains elements of the universal set not in A. A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets. For two sets, n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B). Venn diagrams represent these relationships and solve survey problems.
keyPoints: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)
A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets

material.heading: Number systems
material.body: Natural numbers (1, 2, 3 …) ⊂ integers (…, −1, 0, 1 …) ⊂ rational numbers (p/q, q ≠ 0) ⊂ real numbers, which also include irrational numbers such as √2 and π whose decimals neither terminate nor repeat. Recurring decimals are rational (0.333… = 1/3). Surds are simplified by removing square factors, e.g. √50 = 5√2, and rationalised by multiplying by a conjugate.

topics.title: Indices and Logarithms
topics.summary: Laws of indices, logarithms and exponential equations.

material.heading: Laws of indices
material.body: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1; a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ; a^(1/n) = ⁿ√a; a^(m/n) = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. These rules also underlie scientific notation, e.g. 3.2 × 10⁻⁵.

material.heading: Logarithms
material.body: If aˣ = N then logₐN = x. Laws: log(MN) = log M + log N; log(M/N) = log M − log N; log Mⁿ = n log M; logₐa = 1; logₐ1 = 0. Change of base: logₐN = log N / log a. Logarithms appear in pH (−log[H+]), the decibel scale and first-order drug elimination (ln 2 / k = half-life).

topics.title: Equations and Inequalities
topics.summary: Linear and simultaneous equations, quadratics and inequalities.

material.heading: Linear and simultaneous equations
material.body: A linear equation has the unknown to the first power. Simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns are solved by substitution, elimination or graphically (the intersection of two lines). A straight line has equation y = mx + c, where m is the gradient (m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)) and c the y-intercept.

material.heading: Quadratics and inequalities
material.body: A quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0 is solved by factorisation, completing the square or the formula x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a. The discriminant b² − 4ac tells us: > 0 two real roots; = 0 one repeated root; < 0 no real roots. Sum of roots = −b/a; product = c/a. When multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.
keyPoints: Discriminant decides the nature of roots
Reverse the sign when multiplying by a negative

topics.title: Sequences, Series and Percentages
topics.summary: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, ratios, percentages and simple growth/decay.

material.heading: Progressions
material.body: An arithmetic progression (AP) has a common difference d: nth term Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d; sum Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d]. A geometric progression (GP) has a common ratio r: Tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹; Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) for r ≠ 1; the sum to infinity S∞ = a/(1 − r) when |r| < 1.

material.heading: Percentages and ratios in health
material.body: Percentage change = (change ÷ original) × 100%. Ratios compare quantities (e.g. drug dilution 1:1000 means 1 g in 1,000 mL). Exponential decay describes drug elimination: after each half-life the amount halves, so after n half-lives the fraction remaining is (½)ⁿ. Bacterial growth by binary fission is geometric: N = N₀ × 2ⁿ after n generations.

topics.title: Introduction to Differentiation and Integration
topics.summary: Limits, derivatives of polynomials, rates of change, and basic integration.

material.heading: Differentiation
material.body: The derivative dy/dx measures the rate of change of y with respect to x — the gradient of the tangent to a curve. Power rule: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹; the derivative of a constant is 0. Also d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ, d/dx(ln x) = 1/x, d/dx(sin x) = cos x. Stationary points occur where dy/dx = 0; if d²y/dx² > 0 the point is a minimum, if < 0 a maximum.

material.heading: Integration
material.body: Integration is the reverse of differentiation. ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C (n ≠ −1); ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C. A definite integral ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx gives the area under the curve between x = a and x = b. In pharmacokinetics, the area under the plasma concentration–time curve (AUC) measures total drug exposure.
keyPoints: Definite integral = area under the curve
